inventory_boundary.marker_scan_definition: Plain-text files (no NUL byte) whose content contains 'copyright', 'license' or 'spdx' case-insensitively, measured over every file of the inventory result tree outside the scope exclusions. An earlier unqualified scan counted 26 by matching binary payloads too; see totals.false_positive_note. The scan matches the word wherever it appears, grant or mere reference, so prose that names the checker moves the count: .github/workflows/usdrig.yml joined the set when CI started invoking tools/check_licenses.py, and docs/concepts/licensing.md joined it with its summary line in the generated docs/index.md catalog.

inventory_boundary.count_scope: Every count is measured on the inventory result tree: the 1785 tracked files of base_commit plus tools/license_manifest.json (original-build-and-tooling), docs/legal_members.py and docs/concepts/licensing.md (original-documentation) and tests/testRigExecLegalPackaging.py (original-test-suites). categories.original: authored by the project; root MIT license applies
categories.derived: built from a named upstream source and keeps that upstream's terms
categories.bundled: third-party material carried in the tree or shipped in an artifact
categories.generated: machine output of a checked-in generator or external tool; origin class is the fact, the license grant comes from the inputs
categories.unresolved: no provenance evidence in the repository; owner confirmation required before any automatic blessing

precedence.rule: A path belongs to the family with the lowest precedence number whose globs match it, after that family's carve_outs are applied. Ties are impossible because each family's glob set is disjoint by carve-out. A path matching nothing falls to the precedence-6 fallback.
precedence.verification: The 29 families below partition the 1790 files of the inventory result tree exactly once: 1790 assigned, 0 unassigned, 0 double-assigned, 0 in fallback-unclassified. Verify with tools/check_licenses.py, which re-derives the partition from the checkout.

prose_references.why: Cites public method references. A citation identifies a technique; it is not a license text and is never checked against a vendored file.
Narrates the OpenRigLogic port provenance and points at the pinned commit. The MIT text it explains is quoted in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, not in this file.

The notice names the checker that produced this manifest. It is installed with the binaries but is not a member of the tutorial archives, so the link resolves only in the source checkout or an install prefix.

checker_rules.path_form: Every path in this manifest is repository-relative, has no leading slash, and contains no '..' segment. An add-on source is the exception: it starts with '../' and names the add-on checkout passed explicitly to the packer.
checker_rules.source-form: A distribution legal_members source is either a repository-relative path or '../<add-on-name>/...'. A source that is prose, such as 'addon checkout copy', is a manifest error: the packer refuses to write bytes for it rather than guessing a file.
checker_rules.addon-binding: An add-on source resolves only inside the add-on root supplied at run time (docs/package_godot_example.py --addon-root). A source that leaves that root is rejected before any file is read.
checker_rules.link-resolution: Every relative link in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md must name a file that exists in the checkout, and must reach a member of the install prefix or of the archive that carries that notice, unless the link target is listed in prose_references.
checker_rules.self-reference: tools/license_manifest.json is a provenance record, not a licensed text. A checker may read it, but it never hashes it as part of a legal-text digest and never compares a copy of itself inside an archive against the manifest: the manifest's own bytes change whenever the inventory is refreshed.
checker_rules.existence: Each required_texts path entry, every path in inventory_boundary.archive_members_inventory and every source path in distribution legal_files and distribution legal_members must exist at the recorded boundary; zero matches for any non-fallback family glob or glob in a family's carve_outs is a manifest error. Add-on-bound sources are checked only when the add-on checkout is supplied.
checker_rules.partition: Families must be disjoint. For each tracked file, take the lowest-precedence family whose globs match and whose carve_outs do not exclude it; the result must cover all tracked files exactly once.
checker_rules.no-auto-bless: A family with category unresolved must never be reported as licensed, and its SPDX must stay null until an owner answer is recorded here.
checker_rules.binary-scan: Marker scanning must not run on binary payloads without decoding, or it reports false positives (see totals.false_positive_note).
checker_rules.generated-origin: Generated families are audited through their generator and inputs; the absence of a license header in a generated file is not a violation.
checker_rules.archive-identity: Compare archive legal members after normalizing CRLF to LF, and flag content-stale members rather than treating line endings as drift.
checker_rules.required-text-form: Every required_texts entry is an object with exactly one of path, url or prose. A bare string is a manifest error: a path entry is checked for existence in the tree, a url entry is an upstream text that is deliberately not vendored and is never checked against the filesystem, and a prose entry names documentation that is explicitly a source-only reference and is never expected in an install prefix or an archive.

count_scope: Every count is measured on the inventory result tree: the 1785 tracked files of base_commit plus tools/license_manifest.json and tools/check_licenses.py (original-build-and-tooling), docs/legal_members.py and docs/concepts/licensing.md (original-documentation) and tests/testRigExecLegalPackaging.py (original-test-suites). Each family's matched_files is measured on that same tree.
